leverage.exposure: This is the item that outranks everything else. Cash is effectively nothing and the two live offers together commit far more than the balance holds, so both landing puts the account well into the red. A negative balance at matchday start scores zero for the whole matchday, and the sale allowance rule means the escape route is narrow rather than wide: exactly one combination of sales gets the balance back above zero, and it requires both Lokonga and Sylla to go. The margin is real but thin, and it erodes over time because the market values of the sale candidates are drifting down — Bernardo's fastest of all, which is precisely why he is a poor last-resort funding leg and why, if he ever is needed, he should be sold early rather than late. The reversal on Vagnoman follows directly from this: at his price he would force a third sale onto a margin too small to survive four days of value decay, in exchange for a marginal upgrade the cheaper signing already delivers.

binding_gap: The binding constraint this run is not a position on the pitch, it is unwind capacity. Sale allowance equals the number of buys made, which creates a trap worth understanding before it bites: if the Eggestein offer lands but the Maluze bid loses, only one sale is permitted and no single sale in the squad is large enough to bring the balance back to zero. The fix is cheap and self-healing — buying any inexpensive outfield body immediately grants the second sale — and there is time to react, so this is something to watch rather than pre-empt. One trap to avoid while doing it: the cheapest body on the board is a reserve goalkeeper, and a second keeper wastes the only slot it can fill, leaving too few outfield players to fill any legal formation at all. Take an outfield body if one is ever needed.

verdict.headline: The squad is unchanged and still exactly fieldable with no cover, but the position has quietly become a balance problem rather than a shopping problem.

verdict.detail: The squad is unchanged and still exactly fieldable with no cover, but the position has quietly become a balance problem rather than a shopping problem. Two offers are live — Maluze and Eggestein — and cash is almost nil, so if both land the balance goes deeply negative and has to be unwound before the matchday lock or the entire matchday scores zero. Because the game permits exactly as many sales as buys made, the arithmetic collapses to a single workable route: if both offers land, sell Sambi Lokonga and Sylla, and no other pair of sales clears zero. That single fact drives every other decision this run, and it is why the standing recommendation to chase Vagnoman is reversed.

sell.reason: Sambi Lokonga and Sylla are the pair to sell, in that order of certainty, and they are the only pair whose combined proceeds clear the hole the two live offers create. Lokonga remains a quality sale rather than an availability one — he is fit and played the full match on matchday one, so nothing about his selection has changed; he simply returns too little for what he costs. Sylla carries a second, harder reason: his exit from Schalke is live in dated reporting, with the asking price cut and the club under financial pressure, and although no concrete buyer had emerged twenty-four hours before the real-world window shuts, a player who leaves the league vanishes from the squad entirely. Selling him ahead of that deadline removes the risk for free. Widmer stays a designated sale on merit — he is absent from the newly published probable eleven for matchday two — but he raises too little to function as a funding leg. Bernardo is downgraded to a last resort, and the reasoning behind his sale is corrected below.

Robin Hranac's Ligainsider profile carries no dated news at all since before August 2026, so the substitution cannot be read as a positional demotion; Ligainsider's Hoffenheim page instead has Prass injured and lists Gendrey as the other left-side option, and Bernardo was declared available again on 28.08.2026 after being held out 22.08 as "leicht angeschlagen", then started MD1. No MD2 left-back call exists anywhere dated - no club has published an XI. So the real and only solid case for selling is financial, not selection: mv 6.547.852 with sdmvt -1.013.483, i.e. falling ~1M/day, and he is the 4th-worst scorer at ap 61. DEMOTED to third funding leg behind Lokonga and Sylla and explicitly NOT needed if those two land - the Lokonga+Sylla pair alone clears the hole at +2,33M. Sell him only if a third buy forces a third sale, and if so sell EARLY: every day of delay costs ~1M of proceeds.

buy.reason: Hold both live offers exactly as placed and raise neither. Maluze is the standout: verified fit, a full debut start with an assist and a contract extension announced the same week, and by a wide margin the best points return per euro on the board — he displaces Widmer from the eleven and the bid sits comfortably above the highest premium this league has ever cleared, which is the correct way to bid a blind auction on a cheap player. Eggestein is verified starting in central midfield after a full ninety in a comfortable win, and the offer sits at market value against an ask that has gone unsold for a week; manager asks here clear in the low single digits, so market value is a defensible bid on a stale listing and raising it only worsens the unwind. Ljubicic, carried over as an unverified watch, now checks out cleanly — fit, started matchday one, no suspension — but is avoided anyway: weak scoring for the money, a home fixture against Bayern, a position already covered, and capacity the balance cannot spare. Everything else new on the board is priced far above the measured manager-ask clearing band for players scoring little or nothing.

HOLD the bid, do not raise.

killed_this_run.name: Vagnoman
killed_this_run.why: REVERSAL of BUY Boleuh6 and RAISE Rf17mrr, both now closed unexecuted (no bid was ever placed - ofc=0 on the listing). Verified fit: full 90 at Bayern MD1, Hoeness backed him 29.08.2026 - but that same Ligainsider piece says he is NOT a guaranteed starter, only "needed urgently" with Assignon and Nartey injured. The reversal is not about him, it is about the unwind. Cash is 100.941 and live offers on Maluze (1,20M) + Eggestein (16,31M) already put the balance at -17.404.868 if both land. N buys permit exactly N sales, and with 2 buys the ONLY sale pair that clears zero is Lokonga+Sylla (19,73M -> +2,33M); every other pair leaves him negative at the lock = ZERO points for all of MD2. Adding Vagnoman at 8,30M (+19,88% over mv) forces a 3rd sale that must be Bernardo, whose mv is falling ~1M/day, on a margin of ~480k over four days. And the job Vagnoman was bought for is already done cheaper: Maluze ap 184 at 1,20M displaces Widmer ap 29. Vagnoman would only displace Bernardo ap 61 for +12 ap at 8,30M. Bad points-per-euro and it endangers the whole matchday.

movers.reason: The flip window is technically open, but the mechanism is not there: no manager is asking below market value, so there is no spread to capture. The instant flips visible in the feed this morning were rivals cycling cheap players for a fraction of a percent — motion, not points — and one of them was a defender carrying a fresh ankle injury. Nothing here clears its cost, and with the balance already committed, tying up capacity in a flip would directly threaten the unwind. No action.

fitness.sweep: No squad player is newly injured, suspended or flagged. The good news is concrete: Suzuki scored a hat-trick on matchday one, which confirms his enormous scoring average is real and current rather than a stale artefact, and the season-ending shoulder story about him is confirmed stale. Matsima and Gregoritsch both started and both appear in Augsburg's published probable eleven for matchday two. Guirassy started and scored, Baumann and Minjae both started, and the exit talk around Minjae is reported closed. Widmer's demotion is the one negative and it hardened this run: he is missing from Mainz's probable eleven published today. Two gaps worth stating plainly rather than papering over — nothing dated since late August exists for Nusa, so his fitness is unconfirmed though he is absent from the injured and suspended table; and no club in the league has published a starting eleven for matchday two yet, so every matchday-two starter claim in this briefing is inference from minutes played and dated coach comment, not a confirmed lineup.
